name: Mercury
hook: A liquid metal and the closest planet to the Sun share one name, so the clues split between the two.

facts.label: quicksilver
facts.statement: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature, also called quicksilver; its symbol Hg comes from the Latin for "liquid silver," and Pliny called it argentum vivum.

facts.label: the barometer
facts.statement: Around 1644 Evangelista Torricelli used mercury in a glass tube to invent the barometer, a device for measuring atmospheric pressure.

facts.label: the thermometer
facts.statement: Fahrenheit began using mercury in thermometers around 1715, and in 1866 Thomas Allbutt invented a six-inch clinical thermometer that used it.

facts.label: freezing mercury
facts.statement: In 1759 Braun and Lomonosov used snow and acid to freeze mercury, showing the liquid metal could become solid.

facts.label: the closest planet
facts.statement: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun; it is named for the Roman messenger god, whose Greek counterpart is Hermes.

facts.label: the caduceus
facts.statement: The caduceus — the staff of Mercury or Hermes with snakes — became a common symbol of the medical profession.
